finding.claim: Embed HTML returned by the remote-fetch adapter is emitted unescaped, bypassing html_input, so an attacker-controlled page could inject script when an https URL sits alone on a line.
finding.source: Standalone https:// URL line in untrusted Markdown; attacker controls content served at that URL

trace.note: Parses link destination; requires the whole line to be the URL (line 47)
Top-level embeds passed to adapter updateEmbeds()
Stores $extractor->code->html from remote site as embed code

finding.guards_checked: html_input (Environment.php:434) is only applied in HtmlBlockRenderer/HtmlInlineRenderer, not EmbedRenderer; DisallowedRawHtml does not cover this node; adapter performs no sanitization; DomainFilteringAdapter skipped when allowed_domains is empty (EmbedExtension.php:39). Plausible but unverified: embed/embed library not vendored, so whether code->html can carry attacker script is unconfirmed.

finding.claim: The domain allowlist validates the host with PHP parse_url() but the embed library fetches the raw string and follows redirects, so a parser differential (e.g. backslash before @) or an allowed-host redirect could reach a non-allowlisted host.
finding.source: https:// URL in untrusted Markdown, e.g. https://evil.example\@allowed.example/x
finding.sink: Server-side fetch by the embed library of the unvalidated raw URL (DomainFilteringAdapter passes same string at line 37)

trace.note: Wraps adapter in DomainFilteringAdapter when allowed_domains non-empty
Same raw URL passed to decorated adapter, which fetches it

finding.guards_checked: Scheme restricted to http/https (line 47); host exact/suffix match (line 55); EmbedStartParser requires https:// prefix. Redirect targets are not re-checked. Backslash differential unverified: depends on the embed library's URL handling, which is not vendored.

finding.claim: With allowed_domains left at its default empty list, no domain filter is applied, so untrusted Markdown can make the server fetch any https host, including internal names, with no private-address blocking.
finding.source: Any standalone https:// URL in untrusted Markdown

trace.note: Filter only applied when list non-empty, so skipped by default

finding.guards_checked: No private/loopback address blocking; allowlist is name-based only (no DNS pinning, cf. case 12). Only reachable if an integrator enables the Embed extension with an adapter and leaves allowed_domains at default.

finding.claim: Default configuration permits raw HTML (html_input=allow) and javascript: links (allow_unsafe_links=true), so untrusted Markdown rendered with defaults can produce XSS. This is a configuration default, not a code defect.
finding.source: Untrusted Markdown text containing raw HTML or [x](javascript:...) links
finding.sink: Rendered HTML output (HtmlBlockRenderer.php:46, HtmlInlineRenderer, LinkRenderer.php:48-50, ImageRenderer.php:50-51)

trace.note: Unsafe-link check skipped when allow_unsafe_links is true

finding.guards_checked: RegexHelper::isLinkPotentiallyUnsafe (RegexHelper.php:251-259) correctly handles tab/newline/control-byte obfuscation and blocks svg/non-image data URIs, but only when the option is set to false. Exploitability depends on the consumer's configuration.
